adjudications.justification: signatures.md L42-L43 is the Architecture lead-in ('UCP uses HTTP Message Signatures (RFC 9421) for all HTTP-based transports') — a mechanism statement with no keyword. The MUST is inferred from the section's operative requirements (the Signing requests / Verification MUSTs, SIG-010..SIG-018, SIG-036..SIG-038) which all presuppose RFC 9421 as the only signature mechanism; a non-RFC-9421 signature cannot verify, so the choice is itself observable and is already graded by both lanes (merchant CHECK at 2026-04-08, agent verifier). Kept MUST (decision 29); not a downgrade candidate.

signatures.md L226 is step 3 of the numbered Key Rotation procedure under the lead-in 'To rotate keys without service interruption:' (no keyword). The floor '(minimum 7 days)' is stated as a requirement of the interruption-free procedure; MUST inferred because a verifier that drops an old key earlier than the floor fails signatures the procedure guarantees will verify. Kept MUST for D1-15/D3-23; flagged as a D2-11b downgrade candidate (procedural guidance) — needs-receiver either way.

shopping/catalog/index.md L376 (Common Scenarios / Empty Search): 'When search finds no matches, return an empty array without messages.' — an imperative sentence with no keyword. MUST inferred from the imperative mood in a normative section and from CAT-020's envelope rule (application outcomes return HTTP 200 with the UCP envelope); an implementation that returns an error message for an empty search contradicts the stated behaviour. Kept MUST (decision 29).

shopping/catalog/rest.md L479-L482 (Product Not Found): 'the server returns HTTP 200 with ucp.status: "error" and a descriptive message. This is an application outcome, not a transport error' — descriptive present tense, no keyword. MUST inferred: the sentence defines the only conforming response to an unresolvable identifier (HTTP 200 + error envelope, never a 404), consistent with CAT-020. Kept MUST (decision 29).

payment/extensions/split-payments.md L95 to L100 (the `source` anchor cites L95; the quoted clause runs through L100): '**Matching algorithm:** a submission matches a combination if there exists an assignment of each submitted instrument to exactly one group such that' plus the two itemised conditions at L98 to L100. NOT `pseudocode`: that class is 'every cited line sits inside a code fence', and none of L95 to L100 is fenced (the first fence in the file opens at L111), which is why the mechanical classifier returned None and queued the row instead of classing it. Classed `definition`: the sentence defines the predicate 'matches' that the validity rule at L86 invokes ('A set of instruments is valid if it matches **any** combination in the array'), so it fixes the accept or reject outcome a Business must produce. Kept MUST (decision 29), and left visible as the downgrade candidate the `definition` class carries. checkout-rest.md L188 to L189 (the register cited L188 alone; corrected to the span the quote occupies): Each PUT replaces the entire session, so clients must include all previously set fields they wish to retain. The must is lower case, outside the all caps keyword class the suite accounts by (common/keywords.py), which is why the mechanical classifier queued the row. `inferred`: the sentence is directive, it introduces the Update Buyer Info example in the Update Checkout section, and the replacement rule it states is the one checkout.md L318 gives for Update Checkout with a keyword (CHK-006, the platform is REQUIRED to send the entire checkout resource); a business that merges instead of replacing, or a platform that omits fields it wishes to retain, produces a session state the specification says does not occur. Kept MUST (decision 29) for both roles the row names.

checkout.md L324 to L327 (the register cited L329, which is inside the following MAY sentence; corrected to the span the quote occupies): The response of this call is the checkout object with the order field populated in it. The returned order provides necessary identifiers, such as id and permalink_url, that can be used to reference the full state of the placed order. `definition`: the sentence defines the response of Complete Checkout; order is not in the required list of checkout.json, so the obligation to populate it on completion rests on this sentence alone, and a completion response without order leaves the platform no handle on the placed order. The identifiers are schema facts once order is present (order.json L26 requires id and permalink_url), so the such as in the quote carries nothing the row relies on. Kept MUST (decision 29); the downgrade flag of the class is not exercised, the official CheckoutLifecycleTest asserts order, order.id and order.permalink_url on completion.

checkout.md L269 to L270 (the register cited L273, a blank line under the next heading; corrected to the span the quote occupies): the last item of the Business list (L259) under Guidelines (L238), After a checkout session reaches the state completed, it is considered immutable. NOT `bullet`: that class is a list item under a keyword lead in, and the lead in here is the bare label Business with no keyword; the siblings (L261 to L268) each carry their own MUST or SHOULD, which shows the author keyworded items one by one and left this one in the indicative. `definition`: the item defines the completed state as immutable, a property of the state machine rather than an instruction to a party, and the MUST that follows completion (confirmation email, L261) presupposes a session that no longer changes. Kept MUST (decision 29): the official CheckoutLifecycleTest asserts that update, cancel and a second complete on a completed session do not return 200, so the property is graded as conduct. The downgrade flag of the class records that the author chose no keyword here while keywording every sibling. The same text at 2026-08-25 is CHK-017, labelled bullet in the 2026-09-11 batch, a justification the 2026-09-22 human review found did not survive a reading of its anchor; this entry does not repeat that label.

discount.md L313 to L314 (the register cited L314 alone; corrected to the span the quote occupies): The code still appears in discounts.codes (echoed back) but not in discounts.applied.
